notes.brief_deviation_spread: Brief formula matte' = min(1, matte / (1 - spread)) is NOT implemented: applied to the matte before the blur it is the identity for a binary layer alpha (so spread would do nothing), and applied after the blur it is a different model. Implemented instead the structure of Krita libs/image/layerstyles/kis_ls_drop_shadow_filter.cpp (read as a behaviour reference only, GPL, no code copied): spread_px = spread * size is grown as a hard disc dilation (Krita: Gaussian of spread_size then hard edge), blur_px = size - spread_px by Gaussian, then offset, then knockout. Spread 1 = hard matte grown by the full size; spread has no effect at size 0 (matches the Adobe community thread 'spread not working ... only shadows with hard edges'). Lead may reverse; only effect_math::reference_matte (DropShadow arm) and shadow_split change. Hand tests: tests/effects.rs drop_shadow_offset_blur_taps_and_spread.
notes.brief_acceptance_note_stroke: Acceptance 4 says the 8-neighbour ring is coverage 1 at distance 1. Under the Euclidean model the 12 edge-adjacent ring pixels are exactly 1 and the 4 corner pixels are 1.5 - sqrt(.5) = 0.79289 (round corners), 0 at distance >= 2; inside gives the 8-pixel inner ring exactly. Photoshop's outside-stroke corner shape is UNVERIFIED (D5 13).
formula_sources: Krita libs/image/layerstyles/kis_ls_drop_shadow_filter.cpp (spread_size = (spread*size+50)/100, blur_size = size - spread_size, pipeline spread -> blur -> contour -> noise -> offset -> knockout via erase of the pre-blur selection)

spec_questions: STU-RAS-157 drop_shadow lists spread with unit pixels (observed 0..100) while Photoshop's spread is a percent of size; pigment takes spread as a fraction in [0,1] (composite lowers percent / 100); spec should state the unit

Kind order versus list order: pigment fixes placement by kind (shadow behind; overlay and stroke over) and renders list order within each placement; interop-psd builds lists in Photoshop order; STU-RAS-156 says render order follows list order but does not say whether a shadow listed after an overlay may sit above the content

STU-RAS-157 declares no hard maximum for size, distance and instance count: pigment bounds are engineering limits (size 1000 px vs 213 observed, distance 30000 px = observed maximum, 64 per layer and 4096 per envelope vs 10 per kind minimum) and refuse with typed errors
